findings.claim: DUP_IN_DROPBOX is assigned to every copy of a duplicated hash, so content that exists only in Dropbox is never surfaced as MISSING; the reference tool labels the first copy MISSING and only later copies DUP_IN_DROPBOX.
findings.evidence: classify_hash.py: `elif len(dup.get(h,[]))>1: tier='DUP_IN_DROPBOX'` fires for all copies. tools/dropbox_reconcile.py cmd_classify checks `h in first_by_hash` and only records first_by_hash after classifying, so copy 1 falls through to MISSING. Data: phase3.tsv has 146 DUP_IN_DROPBOX rows = 50 distinct hashes (2,434,137 distinct bytes), 0 of which are in git_index.json, yet SUMMARY.json reports MISSING = 28 files. The by-tier bytes make DUP_IN_DROPBOX (5.4 MB) look like a 'found' tier.
findings.fix: Sort copies by path; give the first copy the next tier down (NAME_SIZE_DIFF_BYTES or MISSING) and label the others DUP_IN_DROPBOX with locator 'copy of <first copy hash prefix>'. Alternatively keep all-copies labelling but add `distinct_contents_not_in_git` (MISSING + DUP distinct hashes + IMPORT_SEEN) to SUMMARY.json and state in a README that DUP_IN_DROPBOX bytes are not in Git.

findings.claim: IMPORT_SEEN sits above DUP_IN_DROPBOX and MISSING in the 'strongest first' order although none of its 21 files has its bytes preserved anywhere in Git; two of them are the import's own not-importable set.
findings.evidence: phase3.tsv IMPORT_SEEN locators: 19 x 'manifest:PUBLISHED_EXTRACTED_TEXT' (Git holds connector text, not the original bytes; the MANIFEST hash is of the original) and 2 x 'not_imported:binary_or_archive' (nothing preserved). Any PUBLISHED_EXACT_ORIGINAL file is already caught by GIT_EXACT (5 rows), so IMPORT_SEEN can only ever hold non-preserved files. The PR directory has no README defining the tier.
findings.fix: Rename to IMPORT_TEXT_ONLY for PUBLISHED_EXTRACTED_TEXT and classify not_imported rows as MISSING with flag IMPORT_LISTED:<reason>; or demote IMPORT_SEEN below DUP_IN_DROPBOX and define it in a README as 'bytes not in Git; the 2026-09-27 import recorded this hash'.

findings.claim: The public-folder test is a token regex over free text (README prose, 5,603 board-comment bodies including ids and timestamps, 459 of them from Math-) with no minimum length, so short or common-word folder names are declared public by coincidence.
findings.evidence: Folder '00' passed via gitpaths token '…/00 — PRIORITY OPEN MAT…' and bodies '17:00:12Z'; folder 'csv' passed via README 'NOT_IMPORTED.csv' and bodies '[dropbox file name withheld]' (lookbehind allows '.'). Both are harmless names, but a Dropbox folder named e.g. 'Medical', 'Family' or a first name would pass whenever that word occurs in any comment. No currently public folder relies solely on bodies.tsv, so that source adds nothing today.
findings.fix: Drop README prose and bodies.tsv from the corpus; test exact path-component equality against Git paths, import-list paths and (per P1) archive member components; require len(base)>=6 for any regex fallback; record the reason per folder in SUMMARY.json so reviewers can audit the decision.

findings.claim: The final guard regexes miss a Dropbox rev hex string, www.[dropbox-site] share links, bare or hex namespace ids and any generic URL; and the guard runs after the files are already written into the PR worktree.
findings.evidence: Tested locally: '015f8a2c3b4d5e6f0000000000f7b1ec5e', 'rev\t015f…' (TSV column), '"rev": "…"', 'https://www.[dropbox-site]/scl/fo/…?[rlkey]…', 'https://www.[dropbox-site]/s/…', 'namespace <namespace>', 'ns:<namespace>a1b', 'https://example.com/…?token=…' all MISSED; only ns:<6+ digits>, [download-host], id:<10+ chars>, 'rev:'/'rev=' and *.google.com are caught. Current protection is structural (phase2_collect/harvest store only size+content_hash), so the guard is defence in depth only. `assert not bad` fires after OUT is populated, leaving leaking files in dbxpr/wt.
findings.fix: Add patterns: r'dropbox\.com/', r'[rlkey]', r'https?://', r'\b[0-9a-f]{9,}[0-9a-f]*\b' outside the content_hash/sha256 columns (or check per column), r'\b1465\d{6,}\b' and a hex form of the namespace id; build OUT in a scratch dir and move it into the worktree only after the guard passes.

findings.claim: git_index coverage is narrower than PINS.json ('main: all refs as fetched') implies: the main clone is shallow (8 shallow boundaries, origin/main history cut at 2026-09-30, 1053 commits) and only two repositories were indexed whereas the 2026-09-27 import compared ten account repos, so a Dropbox file identical to a pre-2026-09-30 version of a since-modified main file, or to a blob in one of the other eight repos, is tiered MISSING or DUP_IN_DROPBOX although it is in Git.

findings.fix: Run git fetch --unshallow (or fetch --deepen) on main before index-git and re-index; either index the other eight account repos or define MISSING in README/SUMMARY as 'not in main (fetched refs, history from 2026-09-30) or Math-'; have cmd_index_git emit the shallow boundary and ref list into the index metadata.

findings.claim: phase2_collect.py line 11 accepts any 64-character third column (no hex check), does not require the path to exist in inventory.tsv, and does not compare size with the inventory; classify_hash.py (line 51) only flags SIZE_CHANGED_SINCE_LISTING and still tiers on the hash (lines 40-45), so a row-shifted subagent TSV (hash of file B under path A) would yield a false GIT_EXACT when B is in Git, detectable only if sizes differ and then only as a flag.

findings.claim: IMPORT_SEEN (line 42) is listed among the 'strongest first' tiers above DUP/MISSING, yet every current IMPORT_SEEN row resolves to PUBLISHED_EXTRACTED_TEXT or NOT_IMPORTED binary_or_archive, i.e. the bytes are in no Git blob; the tier name suggests preservation it does not establish.

result.notes: Review lens: hash rule and index correctness; read-only, no Dropbox/Drive/GitHub tool calls, no files modified, writer scripts not executed (only my own read-only python3 -I checks). Verified non-defects: (1) Hash rule identical. idx/zip_index.py dbx() and tools/dropbox_reconcile.py dbx_hash_bytes() both hash the concatenated SHA-256 digests of 4 MiB blocks; empty input yields sha256(b'') = e3b0c442... in both (2 zero-size git blobs and 82 zero-size archive members carry that value); 53 git_index entries (40 random + all 12 blobs over 4 MiB + both empty blobs) recomputed from local git cat-file: 0 size/sha256/dbx mismatches; index_git.log matches cmd_index_git output format, and all 26672 main index blobs are exactly the blobs reachable from the local clone's refs. (2) Keys line up. content_hashes.json 4472/4472 keys exist in inventory.tsv with equal sizes; list_folder and download_link both return 'ns:<id>//Github/...' and name == basename(path) for all 6000 entries; 83 non-ASCII inventory paths are NFC==NFD (em dash/ellipsis only), 2877 non-ASCII git paths likewise; no path components with edge spaces, no tabs/newlines; 1845 ' (n)' duplicate names are distinct paths. (3) Collect/harvest. Paths with tabs would be rejected by the len(c)!=3 check (no mis-assignment); 4620 subagent rows all well-formed; harvest keys by the ns-stripped path so a hash cannot land on another path, but see F8 for missing hex/size/inventory guards. (4) No symlinks (mode 120000) on any ref tip of either repo, no LFS pointers among indexed blobs, no .gitattributes eol rules (Math- has only '-text' for imports), so CRLF/LFS/symlink cannot produce a false GIT_EXACT; a CRLF Dropbox copy would only produce a false MISSING.
